evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.field: oracle-bone and bronze uses; character formation; competing analysis
evidence.text: The database interprets 干 in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions as a shield, sometimes with upper decoration. It cites an oracle-bone defensive use, 合集 28059「弜令戍干衛」, and bronze 豦簋「干戈」. It also reports the alternative that some oracle-bone 干 and 單 forms are variants depicting a forked hunting implement. These are dictionary interpretations; the underlying glyph images were not visually inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — oraclePiece 干

evidence.source: CASE Press / National Taiwan University science communication
evidence.text: The article identifies the mid-Western Zhou 豦簋 inscription as the earliest securely known 干 in its account. It describes the form as a round shield-like shape with a forked top; later Western Zhou forms change the round upper feature to a short horizontal stroke. That form continues through later scripts, while the forked top is regularized to a shorter horizontal stroke by Eastern Han. The article treats the proposed identification of earlier Shang signs as 干 as disputed and proposes shield ornaments rather than feather decoration for their projections.
evidence.title: 商周時期的防護裝具與兵器：甲、冑、干、盾（四）

evidence.field: 干 formation, historical glosses, and readings
evidence.text: The dictionary quotes the Han Shuowen analysis「犯也。从反入，从一」and gives gān, gàn, and hán readings with senses including offend, shield, seek, and interfere. It separately labels 干 as a variant of 乾 under gān and of 幹 under gàn or hán. This supports distinct lexical readings associated with a shared written form, not an ancient derivation of those words from the shield graph.
evidence.title: A01191 干 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 乾 formation, readings, and textual attestations
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen「上出也。从乙；乙，物之達也。倝聲」and records the fanqie forms 渠焉切 and 古寒切. It distinguishes qián for emergence/upward, heaven, and the trigrams from gān for dry. For dry it cites the *Book of Odes*, 王風·中谷有蓷「中谷有蓷，暵其乾矣」; it also cites parched or dried-up senses in the *Zuo zhuan* and *Shan Hai Jing*. These attestations do not date the first use of the dry word or establish a semantic link to 干 “shield.”
evidence.title: A00044 乾 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.field: Shuowen formation, Guangyun readings, and semantic groups
evidence.text: The entry records Shuowen’s analysis of 乾 as 从乙 with 倝聲 and two Guangyun readings: 古寒切, categorized as 見母, level tone, 寒 rhyme, open division, first grade; and 渠焉切, categorized as 群母, level tone, 仙 rhyme, open division, third grade. The entry’s citations support distinct traditional reading groups for dry and qián/heaven, but do not date their first use or establish their semantic relationship. 倝’s original depicted referent was not established in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 乾

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Characters Database)
evidence.text: The entry treats 幹 as also written 干 in its dictionary discussion and cites 幹 for an implement’s shaft in the *Liji*, a body’s frame in the *Zuo zhuan*, a figurative basis in the *Yi*, and later ability, management, and affairs senses. It gives Guangyun 古案切 and 見母,去聲,寒韻,開口,一等. These examples document uses of 幹; they do not establish an ancient derivation from the shield graph or a phonetic role for 干 inside 幹.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 幹

evidence.text: The dictionary says 幹 is not recorded in Shuowen and describes it as a vulgar form of 榦, with 倝 as the sound element. It records gàn and hán readings and senses including a principal beam or stem, a body’s main part, main/primary, ability, affairs, and to manage. It does not identify 干 “shield” as a semantic or phonetic component in 幹.
evidence.title: A01196 幹 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: file description, source image, and licensing
evidence.text: The exact file 干-seal.svg is described as a modern vector depicting 干 in Shuowen seal-script style. The page identifies its source as image s01611 on hanziyuan.net and lists related database sources. It states that the representation is public domain. This supports the file’s declared identity and reuse status, but the drawing is not an artifact image or evidence for the shield interpretation. The alternate Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg page search result describes a seal-script radical, but opening it failed, so its image, exact identity, and rights were not verified.
evidence.title: File:干-seal.svg — Wikimedia Commons

evidence.field: sources/unihan/Unihan_Readings.txt, kMandarin rows; sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, exact supplied rows
evidence.text: Local Unihan rows read 干 gàn, 乾 qián gān, and 幹 gàn. Exact supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows give 干 MC kan, OC *[k]ˤar (shield row *kˤa[r]); 乾 MC kan, OC *[k]ˤar for dry and MC gjen, OC *[g](r)ar for heaven; and 幹 MC kanH, OC *[k]ˤar-s for stem/framework. These are local-data checks, not evidence by themselves for a graphic or phonetic relationship. Individual Unicode Unihan character records were attempted but inaccessible, so no official character-specific URL is cited for the modern readings.

gaps: The local Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows were checked exactly as supplied, but the individual upstream Unihan pages were inaccessible and no upstream Baxter–Sagart character page was inspected. The local values therefore remain local evidence, not external character-page citations.

The earliest secure 干 attestation reported here is mid-Western Zhou 豦簋; the identification of proposed Shang predecessors remains disputed. No dated artifact glyph was visually inspected in this research.

干’s shield and defensive uses are documented in the cited dictionaries, but their precise chronological sequence is not established. Shuowen’s Han-period “offend/violate” gloss records a historical analysis and does not establish the sense’s origin or development.
乾’s dry use is cited in the *Book of Odes* transmitted text tradition; its first use is not dated. The relation between the dry and qián/heaven words is not established by the inspected sources.

幹’s stem/mainstay and later senses are documented, but an ancient graphic derivation from 干 “shield” is not established. Ministry dictionary instead describes 幹 as a vulgar form of 榦 with 倝 as sound element.

For 倝, the inspected sources report a phonetic role in 乾 and 幹 but do not establish its original depicted referent here. No whole-graph loan claim requiring the shield object’s ancient name was identified.

Commons metadata verifies a modern seal-style vector’s declared character identity, source and public-domain status, but it is not a dated historical artifact and was not used as formation evidence. The exact alternate file page Shuowen Seal Radical 047.svg failed to open.
